title: Webb's illness and wanting to join his band
summary: Jones recalls Webb's kidney ailment and saying he nearly left Basie to learn from the dying bandleader.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Naturally, about Mr. Webb. Mr. Webb gave me

something that could carry me for the rest of my life, because when everybody else was off some place we was off in another place, and he must have known that he was going to die, because I went down to Manhattan Center and Kaiser Marshall was playing the drums. We were back stage.
Kaiser was playing in Chick's band?

Yes. He was listening to the band and he said, "No, Kaiser, not with my band." At that particular time I was almost tempted to leave Basie's band to join Chick Webb's band because of his kidney ailment. I was going to leave Basie's band and play with Mr. Chick Webb out of respect and out of love and at the same time I had a selfish motive. I realized that this man was dying and there were several drummers in New York that never took advantage of being around Mr. Chick Webb and they had been in New York and been around the man longer than I had. But I figured that if I could get any crumbs from the table having a direct contact with this man, I was going to tell Mr. Basie, "I'm going to join Chick Webb's band," and let Chick tell me. After that I followed the band to Washington, D. C. and there was a drummer that when you turned your back his name was Arnold Bolen, "Scrippy", that sounded -
